title: Protection from Violence Manager Ethiopia North Afar
description:
What we’re looking for: Are you passionate about advancing protection and making a tangible difference in the lives of people affected by violence and displacement? NRC Ethiopia is looking for a Protection from Violence (PfV) Project Manager to lead its project portfolio in the North Area Office. This is an opportunity to provide strategic and operational leadership, drive high-quality protection programming, strengthen accountability and ensure effective project delivery in line with NRC standards, strategies and donor requirements. As NRC continues to strengthen and expand its PfV programming across Ethiopia, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering integrated protection interventions across Amhara, Afar and Wolkait Tegede Setit Humera, while contributing to the wider programme's ambitions across the country. Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Female candidates are encouraged to apply. What You Will Do: Here are some of your specific responsibilities: Train, mentor and coach staff delivering specialised protection services, including protection case management and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), in line with NRC modalities, tools and guidance. Promote consistency and alignment of specialised protection activities across field teams and support the development or adaptation of common guidelines, tools and standard operating procedures (SOPs) where required. Ensure that tools and SOPs align with NRC approaches to specialised protection services and that appropriate transition or capacity-development plans are in place where needed. Lead or coordinate area-based, conflict-sensitive analysis and monitoring of protection risks to inform programme design, implementation and adaptation. Ensure that an appropriate case-management tracking system is maintained or established, with due attention to confidentiality, informed consent and data protection. Monitor trends in protection risks emerging from specialised protection services and engage with NRC teams and other protection actors to address risks at community level. Coordinate with the Monitoring and Evaluation team to ensure appropriate monitoring approaches and tools and promote safe monitoring of specialised protection activities. Capture and share lessons learned on project methodology and implementation, and use findings to improve programme quality. Provide technical and managerial support for implementation of specialised protection work plans. Contribute to regional donor reporting, including narrative and financial inputs. Lead the development and design of Civilian Self-Protection (CSP) activities, ensuring that interventions are contextually appropriate and informed by protection analysis. Ensure that learning from CSP implementation is documented and incorporated into programme adaptation and staff development. Please download a more detailed JOB DESCRIPTION for more specific duties and responsibilities. What you will bring: Minimum five years of experience in a senior project implementation or management position in a humanitarian or recovery context. Experience working in complex and volatile contexts. Technical expertise in Protection programming. Demonstrated results relevant to the responsibilities of the position. Knowledge of own leadership skills and profile. Fluency in written and spoken English. Technical expertise and field experience in general protection case management in operation area. Field experience conducting case management and referrals in low-resource settings. Strong interpersonal skills and knowledge of the North Area operational context. Knowledge of local language Experience managing teams and working with IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities. What we offer: Duty station: Afar, Asyita. Contract: 12 months. Travel: Up to 40%. Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions. NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability. We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative. Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC Important information about the application process For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place. When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education. Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV. Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered. We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. If you have any questions about this role, please email ho.recruitment@nrc.no with the job title as the subject line. Why NRC? The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year. Watch this short video to see NRC in action. We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to: do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts. join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility. be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity. About Us The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people. At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. Together, we save lives and rebuild futures. Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to: • treat everyone with respect and dignity • contribute to building a safe environment for all • never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH) • always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Education Project Manager Ethiopia North Afar
description:
What we’re looking for: NRC Ethiopia is seeking a dynamic, experienced and results-oriented Roving Education Project Manager to lead the development and delivery of quality education programmes across its Northern operations. Based in Asayita, you will drive the design, planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of education interventions, spanning rapid emergency education responses, formal and non-formal education, transitional education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). You will play a key role in identifying education needs, developing project proposals, mobilising resources and ensuring that programmes remain responsive to the evolving needs of crisis-affected communities. Working closely with Area Office management, the Country Office Education team, local authorities, consortium partners and other stakeholders, you will provide technical and operational leadership to ensure programme quality, effective resource management, accountability and compliance with donor requirements and humanitarian standards. You will also strengthen team capacity, promote safe and inclusive learning environments, and champion child-friendly feedback mechanisms that expand access to relevant, quality education. We are looking for a leader who can turn education needs into practical, sustainable interventions and help children and young people affected by displacement and crisis - including refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and vulnerable host-community members - access safe, inclusive and meaningful learning opportunities. Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Please download a more detailed JOB DESCRIPTION for more generic & specific duties and responsibilities. What you will bring: Coordinate with Area Office management to ensure the effective planning, implementation, and quality delivery of children and youth programming and foundational education activities. Proper oversight, management and build capacity of education teams to operationalize quality, timely and comprehensive education programming Ensure the effective use of existing monitoring and evaluation systems in collaboration with the Education team, and work with the Country Office to develop, adapt, and streamline Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) tools to strengthen programme quality, responsiveness, accountability, and learning. Promote inclusion, gender and accountability within all education programme Support and contribute to implementation of NRC Education Workstreams and strategies Ensure quality control of education activities through the development and rollout of output and outcome level monitoring and evaluation tools, guidelines and procedures and its timely and proper reporting. Lead the development of project plans, proposals, budgets, and project extensions in collaboration with relevant programme and support teams, ensuring alignment with NRC strategies, donor requirements, and identified needs. title: Expression of interest: Humanitarian Health and Climate Collaborative – Ethiopia Anchor Institution
description:
Overview Elrha is seeking to identify a single anchor institution to act as the national secretariat, operational coordinator and strategic home for the Humanitarian Health and Climate Collaborative (HHCC) in Ethiopia. Ethiopia has been selected as the first national hub, creating an opportunity to establish a credible, country-led mechanism that strengthens local capacity, informs national decision-making and contributes learning to wider regional and global efforts on climate and health in humanitarian crises. Elrha is a global organisation that strengthens humanitarian action by supporting the generation, use and scale of research and innovation that improve outcomes for people affected by crises. The HHCC will bring together public health, climate, humanitarian, research, government and community actors to generate, test and use evidence for more anticipatory and adaptive health action in crisis settings. Objective The anchor institution will provide leadership, convening and operational stability for the Ethiopia hub. It will: National secretariat and coordination: Host the HHCC secretariat, assign core personnel, manage hub operations and act as a trusted convening point across government, academia, meteorological services, humanitarian responders and crisis-affected communities. Governance and priority setting: Establish and convene a national multi-sectoral Steering Group and help identify one or two priority climate hazards for focused collaborative action. Ecosystem scoping and programme design: Lead participatory ecosystem scoping to map evidence gaps, operational challenges, active initiatives, data sources, research questions and innovation opportunities, then co-design the Years 2–5 programme of work. Evidence translation and uptake: Connect climate information with health-sector contingency planning and support the translation of evidence into national policy, planning and frontline humanitarian practice. Grant management readiness: Establish the governance, technical review, financial management and due diligence systems needed to assume devolved research and innovation grant-making responsibilities from Year 2, subject to institutional assessment and systems readiness. Timeline 2 November 2026: invitation for expressions of interest 20 November 2026: Deadline for EOI submissions December 2026: Communication on grant award (expected) December 2026 - January 2027: Due diligence and contracting completed (anticipated) January 2027: Start of grant (anticipated) Funding and opportunity details Opportunity type: Invitation for expressions of interest to become the HHCC Ethiopia Anchor Institution. Programme length: The programme is intended to run from January 2027 to October 2031, subject to funding confirmation. Total programme envelope: Up to £2.4 million with approximately 80% intended for research, innovation and implementation grants delivered through the collaborative platform.

How to Apply: Expressions of interest must be submitted using the structured narrative template provided in **Section 7 of the** [**Expression of interest call** ](https://www.elrha.org/docs/document/expression+of+interest+-+hhcc_ethiopia.pdf?file_url=document/qsqik8hmml60jdpaluf3pdtq7e/ha-coqfi1cwe5fuwxwi-mwas1jy/original?content-type=application%2fpdf&name=expression+of+interest+-+hhcc_ethiopia.pdf)and returned no later than **17:00 UTC on Friday 20 November 2026**. Completed submissions must be sent to: hhcc@elrha.org with the subject line: *EOI SUBMISSION – HHCC Anchor Institution – \[Your Organisation’s Name\]* **Join our drop-in session** On Monday 16 November at 13:00 (UTC) we'll be hosting a live drop-in session to answer any questions you have about this opportunity. You can register for the session[ **here**](https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/ew0BYLO6T4-wBJ5zx3Vrlw#/registration).

title: Chief of Party II, Ethiopia
description:
NOTE: This recruitment is contingent upon donor approval. Job Summary CRS seeks Chief of Party II candidates for the anticipated USDA Non-Emergency Food for Peace projects. These multi‑year, development-focused projects seek to combat chronic and acute malnutrition especially in children and mothers, strengthen early recovery and resilience, and support communities. The Chief of Party II will provide vision, leadership and overall management of these large and complex projects to serve the poor and vulnerable. The incumbent’s strategic leadership, management and technical knowledge will ensure the delivery of high-quality programming and advance the position of CRS as a leading agency in the respective field. As a senior leader, the Chief of Party II will proactively manage security and mitigate security risks. This position will be based in Addis Ababa where CRS has been operating in Ethiopia since 1958. CRS currently implements a portfolio of lifesaving, development, resilience, and peacebuilding programs. CRS works across the country with local partners, government institutions, and communities to address food insecurity, malnutrition, and recovery from recurrent shocks. CRS brings extensive experience managing large-scale food security and resilience programs, including nutrition, agriculture, value chain strengthening, market systems development, livelihoods, and natural resource management interventions. Roles and Key Responsibilities Lead all aspects of the development, implementation and consolidation of the assigned project, including sharing how the project contributes to the thought leadership of the industry. Serve as the primary point of contact with the donor as well as public, private and non-government stakeholders. Ensure the project is designed and implemented to meet donor expectations in terms of timely and quality results and budget, including strategies for phase out and sustainability. Lead coordination efforts between program and operations leads to ensure CRS program quality standards are adhered to. Effectively lead senior programming and operations talent. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching and mentoring. Strategically tailor individual development plans and complete performance assessments for direct reports. Oversee the development of staffing plans and the recruitment process of senior staff. Proactively manage and mitigate risk by monitoring national and regional issues that may impact staff and programming. Ensure all CRS staff safety and security policies and plans are regularly updated and all staff understand and adhere to these policies. Promote, uphold and model a commitment to the efficient use of agency and donor resources. Ensure compliance with donor grants, including financial tracking and oversight of partner budgets, finance, administration and donor reporting. Approve program expenditures, budget adjustments, and cost modification requests to donors. Represent CRS programming in international circles, highlighting innovative work. Publish program results and deliver presentations. Oversee the development of communication strategies and materials, complying with donor and CRS’ branding and marketing requirements and procedures. Manage relationships with consortium partner organizations, including organization of review/planning workshops. Coordinate the roles and activities of staff from other consortium member organizations to ensure implementation is in line with CRS partnership principles. Create and maintain proper conditions for learning. Establish a safe environment to share ideas, solutions, and difficulties. Build the internal capacity to detect, analyze and respond quickly to deficiencies. Identify performance gaps and training opportunities for CRS and partner staff and ensure the design and delivery of high-quality training and technical assistance. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in international development, International Relations or a relevant technical area. Minimum of 8 years’ of relevant management and technical experience. Minimum of 7 years’ experience managing donor funds, including multi country grants. Excellent knowledge and experience in budget management. Minimum of 5 years’ of staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment. Experience coaching and mentoring senior program staff. Demonstrated experience of successful program management, including management of complex, high-value, multi-activity projects, with complicated logistics. Established leader in sector as demonstrated by peer reviewed publications, conference presentations etc. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in a related field. Experience engaging partners and strengthening partnerships. Knowledge of CRS partnership strategy. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Ability to represent and present at high levels. Excellent knowledge of MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems. Excellent strategic, analytical, systems thinking, and problem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment and decisions. Excellent relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Ability to strategically approach each relationship. Team leadership abilities with diverse and multi-disciplinary teams. Coaching/mentoring skills. Strong communication and presentation skills. Ability to develop tailored and persuasive messaging for varied audiences. Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented mindset. Required Languages: Fluency in English is required. Fluency in a local language is a plus. Travel: Must be willing and able to travel up to 35%. Supervisory Responsibilities: Yes Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff): Personal Accountability – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions. Acts with Integrity - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest. Builds and Maintains Trust - Shows consistency between words and actions. Collaborates with Others – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams. Open to Learn – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things. Agency Leadership Competencies: Lead Change – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation. Develops and Recognizes Others – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance. Strategic Mindset – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

How to Apply: Candidates should upload a CV and cover letter to our career page using [this link.](https://eipn.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1/job/3002999/?utm_medium=jobshare&utm_source=External+Job+Share)

title: HEAD OF OFFICE (M/F/D), ETHIOPIA
description:
The German Red Cross (GRC) assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Our Mission: We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape. The GRC is currently seeking an experienced Head of Office (m/f/d) to lead its Country Office in Ethiopia. The GRC has a long-standing partnership with the Ethiopian Red Crescent Society (ERCS). At present, the primary focus of GRC lies in providing assistance to the ERCS in addressing the ongoing crisis and humanitarian needs and adjusting the existing portfolio according to the changing needs and according to ERCS priorities The GRC is committed to support its Sister Society where possible and work with the ERCS team to jointly decide on long-term programmes which fall within ERCS strategic priorities through joint programs, exchange of knowledge as well as technical and managerial support. The Head of Office (HoO) is located in Addis Abeba. He/she directly supervises the international GRC delegates and national staff and is responsible for the overall security management. The HoO reports to the country manager at GRC HQ in Berlin. Starting date: 01.01.2027 Duration: 12 months (with possible extension) Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent visits to the project sites Main duties & responsibilities: Strategic leadership and representation: Lead the GRC Country Office and represent the GRC in Ethiopia vis-à-vis ERCS, the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, government authorities, the German Embassy, donors, national and international humanitarian organisations and other relevant stakeholders. Maintain strong partnerships and networks and contribute to the positioning and visibility of the GRC in the country. Support ERCS in building and strengthening their capacities and programmes in line with the ERCS National Society Development (NSD) strategy. Partnership and Movement coordination: Ensure close coordination and cooperation with ERCS and support the implementation of the IFRC Ways of Working (WoW) localisation initiatives and other efforts to strengthen ERCS capacities. Represent the GRC in relevant Movement coordination platforms, including the MOC, CCT and technical working groups (TWGs), and foster synergies with Movement partners. Country strategy and programme development: Further develop and adapt the GRC country strategy and operational portfolio in line with the evolving humanitarian context, needs assessments and ERCS priorities. Identify funding opportunities and lead or contribute to the development of concept notes and project proposals in coordination with ERCS, GRC Headquarters and Movement partners. Financial and administrative management of the country office: Oversee the financial and administrative management of the Country Office, including budgeting, expenditure monitoring, procurement, human resources, inventories and the management of fixed and financial assets. Ensure that appropriate systems, structures and procedures are in place and implemented in accordance with GRC guidelines and applicable donor regulations, in close coordination with the finance and project delegates. Direct line-management of GRC delegates and support of staff development and capacity building of national and international team. Programme and project management: Oversee the implementation of GRC-supported programmes and ensure high-quality, timely and effective delivery in line with approved objectives, budgets and work plans. Monitor programme progress, assess results and risks, and ensure compliance with GRC policies and donor requirements, including those of BMZ, GFFO and ECHO. Ensure timely and accurate narrative and financial reporting. Where required, directly manage emergency response projects in close coordination with ERCS Headquarters, local ERCS branches, project teams and volunteers. Context monitoring and analysis: Monitor and analyse relevant political, socio-economic, humanitarian and security developments, with a particular focus on humanitarian needs, disaster risks and their implications for GRC operations. effective information sharing with GRC Headquarters and external stakeholders. Security management: Ensure that security policies, procedures and contingency plans are regularly reviewed, updated and followed by all staff. Coordinate security management with relevant Movement partners, and ensure compliance with applicable security arrangements, including the L2 agreement with the ICRC. Leadership and capacity strengthening: Directly supervise and support international delegates and national staff, promoting professional development, team cohesion and a positive working environment. Support ERCS in strengthening its organisational capacities and programmes in line with its National Society Development (NSD) strategy. Ensure communication, visibility and information sharing on GRC/ERCS programmes with all stakeholders, including project beneficiaries, partners, local authorities and donors. Required Competencies & Skills: Technical experience: University degree in a relevant field. At least five years of professional experience in international cooperation, including substantial experience in humanitarian crisis and/or development contexts. Demonstrated experience in programme and project management, including budgeting, financial monitoring, programme quality assurance, monitoring and evaluation, and donor reporting. Experience in staff management, team leadership and capacity strengthening. Previous experience leading a country office for a humanitarian organisation, managing international teams and overseeing security management is an asset. Technical expertise in one or more of the following areas: WASH, shelter and non-food items (NFI), anticipatory action, cash and voucher assistance, health/pre-hospital emergency care (PHEC), food security or livelihoods. Sound understanding of the humanitarian system, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and disaster management. Experience within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement is a strong asset. Substantial experience implementing donor-funded projects. Familiarity with BMZ, GFFO and ECHO funding requirements is a strong asset. Proven experience in organisational development, capacity building and team coaching. Experience working in the Greater Horn of Africa, particularly Ethiopia, is an asset. Personal skills: Excellent leadership, diplomatic, communication, negotiation and networking skills, with the ability to represent the organisation effectively and engage with diverse stakeholders. Strategic thinking combined with a hands-on, pragmatic and solution-oriented approach. Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritise and make decisions in complex and rapidly changing environments. Excellent intercultural sensitivity and the ability to work independently while fostering effective teamwork. Resilience and strong stress-management skills, including the ability to work in insecure and conflict-affected environments. Knowledge of policies and procedures relating to safety and security, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), compliance and human resources development. Fluency in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Amharic and/or German is an advantage. Excellent computer skills, including spreadsheets, word-processing software, databases and other relevant applications. Readiness to travel to and work in remote areas is essential. Experience of living and working in insecure and conflict-affected environments is an asset. Ability to work independently and as a team member; Ability and agreement to adhere to the Red Cross Red Crescent Fundamental Principles; Ability to complete a thorough medical screening process 'working abroad under specific climate and health conditions’; Valid International Driving Permit (IDP). What we offer you: You will be part of a highly motivated professional and multicultural team. We offer you a compensation package according to the collective employment agreement of the GRC, an expatriation allowance during your mission. In addition to a full insurance package GRC is covering a home flight within a 12-months period of assignment. You will benefit from a comprehensive training package and receive briefings and coaching prior as well as during and after your mission. Medical check-ups and Psychosocial Support Service are included in your assignment.

How to Apply: **Kindly apply by submitting your application by using the** [**GRC online application**](https://karriere-beim-drk.de/mv36a) **system until 15.11.2026.** Please note that due to the travel and visa regulations and the guidelines of our partners in the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement certain vaccinations are required for this delegate position. Candidates on the short-list for this position will be asked to disclose their vaccination status. [HEAD OF OFFICE (M/F/D), ETHIOPIA](https://karriere-beim-drk.de/onm87) We point out that the selection and nomination processes for this international delegate position may demand that information concerning your person be shared with involved Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners (IFRC, ICRC, National Society). This may include transmission into countries that do not apply data protection standards comparable to those of the European Union.

title: Regional Safety & Security Director
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Context The East Africa region supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges – conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation – through integrated, impactful approaches. The region prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration. The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. EA focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs. The EA region operates country programs in Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and Ethiopia. Position Summary The Regional Safety and Security Director (RSSD) is one of the most senior leadership roles in the East Africa region and provides strategic leadership for safety, security, and humanitarian access across the region. They set and drive the implementation of a comprehensive strategy to anticipate, analyze, and mitigate risks, safeguard staff and assets, enable principled humanitarian access, and ensure the continuity of IRC’s operations and programs in complex and high-risk environments. As the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the Regional Vice President (RVP), the RSSD works alongside the RVP on the decisions that shape IRC’s presence, access, and continuity across the region. They are a full member of the Regional Management Team and of IRC’s global safety and security (S&S) team. Within the Regional Management Team, the RSSD contributes as a senior leader to regional strategy, priorities, and decision-making, not only as the safety and security function, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices. They integrate Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) informed security risk analysis into strategic, operational, programmatic, and partnership decisions so that security considerations are embedded across IRC’s work. Reporting jointly to the RVP and the Senior Director for Safety and Security (SDSS), the RSSD operates with significant autonomy and influence. Working in close partnership with Country Directors, they ensure that each country program has robust, context-appropriate protocols, systems, and capacities in place to address unique threats and challenges, while remaining agile to adapt to shifting environments. The RSSD maintains in-depth knowledge of security dynamics across all EA countries, monitors early warning indicators, and deploys regularly, including at short notice, to support local teams. They play a central role in mentoring and building the capabilities of IRC staff and leaders to operate safely and effectively, thereby strengthening IRC’s ability to reach and serve the most affected and underserved populations. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Regional Management As a member of the Regional Management Team, contribute as a senior leader to regional strategy, priority-setting, and decision-making, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices across the region rather than representing the safety and security function alone. Serve as the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the RVP, enabling timely, risk-informed decisions on humanitarian access, operational continuity, and duty of care, and jointly activating and leading crisis management when required. Partner with Country Directors to align safety, security, and humanitarian access with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs) and operational priorities, supporting their decision-making and accountability for risk. Security Risk Management Lead and supervise the identification, analysis, and mitigation of S&S risks across the region, ensuring alignment with IRC’s global standards. Guide and support Country Directors and field leaders to adapt and implement context-specific security risk management strategies ensuring proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness. Review, monitor, and encourage compliance with the Security Minimum Standards (SMS) in all country programs providing follow-up and technical guidance where gaps are identified. Drive and champion the development, adaptation, and roll-out of global and regional initiatives on duty of care and safeguarding, embedding these into operational culture and practice. Shape and strengthen safety and security policies, procedures, and practices that fully integrate Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (GEDI) principles as well as Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) commitments. Extend IRC’s security capacity to partners, ensuring they receive tailored risk management support, access to systems, and benefit from IRC’s standards relevant to their operational contexts. Build and maintain an active network of IRC security focal points across country programs and cultivate strong external relationships with professional contacts, peer agencies, and security counterparts to enhance collective risk management. Humanitarian Access Management Enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access across country programs, ensuring communities can be reached and served in line with IRC’s country Strategy Action Plans (SAP). Strengthen and expand humanitarian access teams and capabilities across the region, building skills, systems, and approaches that enhance operational reach and acceptance. Develop, adapt, and implement context-specific guidelines for humanitarian access and engagement with state and non-state actors, ensuring alignment with IRC policy, international humanitarian law, and standards. Advise and guide country programs in the design of operational and programmatic contingency plans ensuring preparedness for sudden shifts in political, security, or conflict dynamics. Collaborate with relevant IRC units to ensure prompt and appropriate follow-up to violations of IRC’s Code of Conduct and breaches of humanitarian principles, reinforcing accountability and ethical operations. Performance Management and Development Lead and actively contribute to the recruitment and selection of key positions with S&S responsibilities, ensuring high-caliber talent and diverse representation. Co-manage and mentor direct-report staff (under the Management in Partnership (MiP) model with Country Directors), setting clear expectations, defining performance objectives, providing regular, timely feedback, and conducting documented performance reviews that drive accountability and growth. Promote and safeguard staff well-being, monitoring staff care across the region and supporting appropriate interventions to address the needs of both national and international staff. Directly supervise and develop the Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Coordinator, ensuring progressive and forward-looking S&S plans that align with regional priorities and organizational strategy. Learning & Development Design, support, and supervise the implementation of regional capacity-building plans, ensuring effective delivery of IRC’s global S&S training programs across EA country programs. Embed gender-sensitive approaches into all capacity development and learning initiatives, addressing gender-specific risks and ensuring inclusivity in staff preparedness. Lead and facilitate critical incident management trainings and simulations, in close coordination with the global S&S unit to strengthen preparedness and response capacities across the region. Incident Management Support country programs to ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality incident notification, reporting, analysis, and dissemination of lessons learned. Serve as a member of the Regional Incident Management Team actively supporting the RVP in the management and resolution of Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents. Facilitate After-Action Reviews ensuring that corrective measures are clearly defined, documented, and systematically implemented in line with established incident protocols. Oversee and monitor the SHIELD incident database producing quarterly trend analyses to inform strategic decision-making and strengthen regional risk mitigation. Key Working Relationships Reports to: Regional Vice President, East Africa, and Senior Director, Global Safety & Security (matrixed reporting) Member of: Regional Management Team and IRC’s global Safety & Security team Partners closely with: the Regional Vice President, as principal safety and security advisor, and Country Directors on country risk, humanitarian access, and duty of care Manages: Regional Humanitarian Access & Security Coordinator; and, through Management in Partnership with the respective Country Directors, country Security Leads Collaborates with: fellow Regional Safety & Security Directors, the Director of Security Learning & Operations, the Global Duty of Care Director, People & Culture, and other members of the Regional Management Team; and, externally, with peer agencies, security networks, and relevant counterparts Qualifications & Requirements At least 10 years’ experience in international humanitarian assistance, with proven ability to plan, organize, and lead security management operations. Prior experience in EA with strong knowledge of regional and country dynamics is essential. Fluency in English required; proficiency in a relevant regional language (e.g. Arabic, Amharic, Somali, or Swahili) is an asset. Demonstrated grounding in humanitarian principles, codes of conduct, NGO culture, and proven success in gender-sensitive security management and gender equality. Skilled at influencing without authority and building effective relationships across multinational teams, partners, and stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge through mentoring, coaching, and non-formal methods. Strong capacity to analyze and present complex security dynamics and incidents clearly and on short notice, highlighting implications for operations. Willingness and ability to travel up to 40% of the time. Work Environment This position is open to both national and international applicants, in the locations indicated as well as potentially other IRC locations open to hosting. We will, however, prioritize consideration of national candidates from the region and for which our highly competitive national salary scale and benefits will apply. Returning National Candidates: We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based, are currently located outside your home country, and possess over 4 years of international work experience, the IRC has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing, and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs. Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: at IRC, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply for this role, and are committed to supporting them through flexible working arrangements, safety and duty of care planning tailored to the East African countries’ context, and a workplace culture that values the leadership women bring to humanitarian response. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Pre-Hospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d)
description:
The German Red Cross (GRC) assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Our Mission: We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape. The GRC is currently seeking a Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d) . The Delegate will advise the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) and the GRC on prehospital emergency care (PHEC) and related health matters. In addition, the Delegate will oversee the implementation of a new project funded under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)’s Social Structure Funding (SSF) programme, in close cooperation with ERCS. The three-year project, entitled “Strengthening the Ethiopian Red Cross Society as a key actor in the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) system and improving the national enabling environment,” is planned to run from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029. It aims to strengthen ERCS’s institutional and technical capacities in Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and contribute to the further development and standardisation of EMS in Ethiopia. Key areas include capacity building, the development and implementation of national guidelines and policies, and strengthening coordination and quality assurance within the national EMS system. The Delegate will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia and work under the supervision of the Head of Office and will be part of an experienced team of three international delegates and local staff. The position is subject to final confirmation of BMZ funding. Starting date: 01.01.2027 Duration: 24 months, with possible extension Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent visits to the project sites Main duties & responsibilities Provide technical advice and contribute to strengthening ERCS capacities in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and related health areas , including through the development and implementation of national standards, guidelines, training approaches and quality assurance mechanisms, capacity building and training-of-trainers approaches, and support to the institutionalisation and sustainability of PHEC and EMS services. Oversee the implementation of the BMZ SSF-funded EMS project in close cooperation with the ERCS, including project planning, reporting and budget management, ensuring effective, timely and quality implementation in line with the approved project proposal, budget and donor requirements. Ensure close coordination with relevant national and international stakeholders , including the Ethiopian Ministry of Health, NGOs, Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners providing technical support to health-related activities, and other actors working in health, particularly in PHEC. Represent GRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups and related clusters. Support project monitoring, learning and quality assurance , including regular monitoring of activities and results, collection and analysis of project data and indicators, identification of implementation challenges, and follow-up on agreed actions. Support the identification and development of opportunities for additional funding for PHEC activities from other institutional and private funding sources. Provide support in emergencies in the area of PHEC and beyond , as requested by ERCS and GRC. Required Competencies & Skills University degree in Paramedicine/Prehospital Emergency Care, Public/Global Health, Health Management, Disaster Management or a related field. A clinical background as a paramedic, emergency nurse or physician with prehospital experience is an asset. At least five years of professional experience in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), emergency care, humanitarian health or a related field. Strong technical knowledge and practical experience in PHEC , ideally including experience in the development or implementation of PHEC systems, standards, guidelines, training programmes, quality assurance mechanisms and/or referral systems. Demonstrated project management experience , including project planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, budget management and financial monitoring of donor-funded projects. Experience with BMZ-funded projects is an asset. Experience in capacity strengthening and adult learning , including the design and facilitation of trainings, workshops and/or training-of-trainers approaches. Previous experience working with the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and knowledge of its structures, approaches and Fundamental Principles are strong assets. Experience in multi-stakeholder coordination , preferably with government authorities, National Societies, international organisations and other health or PHEC actors. Strong communication, coordination and representation skills , with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with partners at different organisational levels. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively in complex and changing environments , with a high degree of cultural sensitivity and adaptability. Excellent written and spoken English . Knowledge of German is an asset. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a multicultural and multidisciplinary team . Ability and agreement to adhere to the Fundamental Principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement . Ability to complete a thorough medical screening process for working abroad under specific climate and health conditions and willingness to travel within Ethiopia as required for project implementation and monitoring. Valid International Driving Permit (IDP) . What we offer you You will be part of a highly motivated professional and multicultural team. We offer you a compensation package according to the collective employment agreement of the GRC, an expatriation allowance during your mission as well as a personal allowance to cover your accommodation. In addition to a full insurance package, GRC is covering a home flight within a 12-month period of assignment. You will benefit from a comprehensive training package and receive briefings and coaching prior to, during and after your mission. Medical check-ups and Psychosocial Support Service are included in your assignment.

All staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of conduct and to protect the rights, dignity, and well-being of the people we serve and work with. Safeguarding responsibilities are integrated into all roles, and all personnel are required to adhere to our rules of conduct and safeguarding policies.* *Recruitment is subject to satisfactory reference and background checks. By submitting an application, candidates acknowledge and agree to provide the requested information and to undergo the relevant checks.* *Please note that due to the travel and visa regulations and the guidelines of our partners in the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement certain vaccinations are required for this delegate position. Candidates on the short-list for this position will be asked to disclose their vaccination status.* *We point out that the selection and nomination processes for this international delegate position may demand that information concerning your person be shared with involved Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners (IFRC, ICRC, National Society). title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
description:
Desired start date: 01/12/2026 Duration of the mission: 6 Months Location: Adwa - Tigray Region SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms. PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

How to Apply: Do you recognize yourself in this description? If yes, please send us your CV and cover letter! Thank you for your understanding. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Education Bachelor's degree required. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 05 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression.
